channel.title: Tensile journal
channel.description: The Tensile journal is where our designers and engineers write about how we work: product design, design systems, websites and the way we run projects. Short, practical, no sales pitch.

item.title: Why we design the empty states first
item.description: The first screen most users see is empty. We start there, and the rest of the product gets better for it.
item.author: hello@example.com (Leah Park)

item.title: A design system is a promise, not a library
item.description: Components are the easy part. The hard part is the promise behind them, and who keeps it after we leave.
item.author: hello@example.com (Inês Moreira)

item.title: How we quote in week two
item.description: We do not quote from a brief. We quote after two paid weeks of discovery, and clients thank us for it.
item.author: hello@example.com (Daniel Sousa)

item.title: How clients read a staging link
item.description: We send a staging link every Friday. After four years of watching what people click, we design the links differently.
item.author: hello@example.com (Jonas Becker)
